elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: The rendered operative text is unchanged from the original: Section 13.5 warrants only that SFJ "will have, as and when needed, sufficient funds to satisfy its obligations hereunder." No professional-and-workmanlike standard for the SFJ Services appears anywhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: No conformance warranty of any kind is present in the rendered text; Section 13.6.2 instead disclaims all warranties except those "SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 13," and Article 13 as rendered contains only the funding covenant.

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: No warranty period appears in the rendered language; the deterministic check "warranty period \u2265 90 days or expressed in months/years" returned ok:false.
No services warranty and therefore no 90-day (or any) duration exists in the rendered text.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: No remedy sentence appears in the rendered operative language; the claimed remedy text is only described in the rationale as mapped to "operation 1," which the coverage gate reports as an invalid/non-existent operation.
No refund remedy is rendered; the mapping again points to invalid operation index 1, so nothing was actually inserted into Article 13.

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Rendered Article 13 text contains no SFJ compliance-with-laws warranty; only the sufficient-funds covenant in 13.5.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code warranty appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Expressly left "unaddressed" by the drafter on the theory that SFJ supplies no software or deliverables. Even accepting that the condition may not apply, nothing conforming was inserted, and the accompanying services warranty that would carry the fallback was also not rendered; per the framework a level cannot be complete where an element is omitted and merely explained in commentary.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Claimed to be "addressed_by_operation" index 1, but the element coverage gate reports "Element references invalid operation 1," and the rendered operative language contains only unchanged Sections 13.5 and 13.6.2 \u2014 no 30-day services conformance warranty exists.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Same defect: mapped to invalid operation 1; no re-performance/repair/replacement remedy is present in the rendered text.
Same defect: mapped to invalid operation 1; no refund-of-fees remedy is present in the rendered text.

reasons: The redline is inoperative: every fallback element is mapped to "operation 1," which the deterministic element-coverage gate reports as an invalid operation, and the rendered operative language is byte-identical to the original Sections 13.5 and 13.6.2. Nothing was actually inserted, so no level is reached.

Repair required: insert an express warranty into Article 13 (so the "EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 13" carve-out in 13.6.2 preserves it) stating that SFJ will perform the SFJ Services in a professional and workmanlike manner and that, for at least thirty (30) days following performance, the SFJ Services will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement / the applicable protocol.

Repair required: add the remedy sentence \u2014 at SFJ's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or refund of amounts paid for the non-conforming SFJ Services \u2014 as neither the repair/replacement nor the refund limb currently exists in operative text.
The deterministic period check failed (no warranty period \u2265 90 days or stated in months/years is present), confirming that no duration term was rendered for either the software or services limb.

On the software element: the drafter's needs_review note that the Agreement supplies no SFJ software, deliverables or documentation is plausible, but it must be resolved in operative language \u2014 either confirm no software exists (and rely on the services limb alone) or insert a 90-day software-to-documentation warranty; the framework does not permit completing a level on an element that is only promised in commentary.
No minimality or intent defect arises because no text was changed, deleted or duplicated; the failure is one of completeness, not of scope.

Severity retained at medium: the clause sits at walk-away (sweeping 13.6.2 disclaimer with no conformance warranty), but the target obligation here is oversight/funding rather than software supply, so no escalation is warranted.
